claim: POST /recurring-orders/:restaurantId (RecurringOrdersService.createRecurringOrder) and PUT /recurring-orders/:restaurantId/:id (updateRecurringOrder) check the body's inventory_id and provider_id against the path house, which JwtAuthGuard requires to be the session's, through the private assertIdsAreThisHouses: create passes both keys, so both are always checked, before its recurring_orders insert; update passes its patch, so only the ids the body sent are checked, before it reads (getRecurringOrder) or updates the schedule. The item check is assertInventoryBelongsToRestaurant (another house's item or a missing id: 403; a failed read: 422). The vendor check is assertProviderBelongsToRestaurant (apps/api-gateway/src/common/tenant/assert-provider-belongs-to-restaurant.ts), ProcurementService.createOrder's inline vendor fence moved there with the same query and answers, and createOrder now calls it before its first provider_id read or write: a providers row counts only when its restaurant_id is the house, so another house's vendor, a vendor row with no house and a missing id get 404 'Vendor not found', and a failed read gets 503. At 1c1a676f8 neither route checked either id: in a two-house harness, create answered 201 naming the other house's wine or vendor and wrote calendar rows in the caller's house that carried it, and update answered 200.
